entries.title: Spanish pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests dies, union says
entries.snippet: Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was forcibly removed on a stretcher from her apartment of more than 70 years in September.

entries.title: Israelis mourn 7 October attack victims three years after deadly Hamas raid

entries.snippet: The step comes after several groups complained of police using disproportionate force towards teenagers.

entries.title: Canada suspends plans to expand assisted dying to people with mental illness
entries.snippet: People with mental illness alone were to be eligible for assisted dying in Canada in March 2027, but that has now been paused indefinitely.

entries.title: Trump to speak to Putin about plague lab worker's death in Russia

entries.snippet: The patient passed through multiple cities in DR Congo, drove to Uganda and eventually flew to Kenya.

entries.title: The WHO seeks more details on the death of a plague research lab employee in Russia
entries.snippet: The World Health Organization says it wants more information on what caused the death of an employee at a Russian plague research lab. Russia says the woman died of pneumonia of unknown origin.

entries.title: What is the pneumonic plague?
entries.snippet: The ancient disease of plague is back in the headlines after the death this month of a Russian lab worker.

entries.title: This surprising mammal fossil is giving scientists something to chew on

entries.title: Judge orders that Christa Pike execution evidence be preserved
entries.snippet: A week after the failed execution, Pike is awake but is said to be angry and confused. Her lawyers said Wednesday's hearing was about "transparency."

entries.title: Trump approved the military's 1st firing squad execution since WWII. Why now?
entries.snippet: The Pentagon says Nidal Hasan will be executed by firing squad in December at Fort Hood, where he killed 13 people in 2009. The announcement came days after a botched lethal injection in Tennessee.

entries.title: Why Trump just loosened the rules on 'dyed diesel' — normally a farm fuel
entries.snippet: Trump is temporarily allowing this fuel to be used on highways, although it's typically just for off-road farm and construction vehicles. Could that lower the price of diesel?

entries.title: How Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has brought the culture wars to the military
entries.snippet: The New York Times reporter Greg Jaffe says Hegseth has disproportionately blocked promotions of Black and women senior officers, and he's also been purging the military of transgender people.

entries.title: She got Trump's $500 check for health insurance. To her, it's a 'political stunt'
entries.snippet: As checks from President Trump for health costs hit millions of mailboxes, a poll shows Americans don't trust Republicans on healthcare. Experts doubt it will move the needle and say it is likely illegal.

entries.title: Gut microbes followed migrating humans across continents, new study suggests
entries.snippet: New research looks at the surprising similarities in the gut microbiomes of hunter-gathers in Tanzania and horticulturalists in Bolivia, and asks: What role do these bacteria play in human health?

entries.title: Greetings from Lahore, Pakistan, whose high court offers an oasis for chatter and chai
entries.snippet: The Lahore High Court is a near-perfect specimen of British South Asian colonial architecture and its main square is a pleasant spot shaded by banyan trees.

entries.title: Student loan borrowers have more time to reduce interest rates. Here's what to know
entries.snippet: The original deadline was Sept. 30, but the U.S. Department of Education extended it to give borrowers more time to enroll. The rate reduction will last through June 2028.

entries.title: Eva Marie Saint, star of 'On the Waterfront' and 'North by Northwest,' dies at 102
entries.snippet: Saint had one of the most spectacular debuts in Hollywood history, as the love interest of Marlon Brando's tormented Terry Malloy in "On the Waterfront."

entries.title: Tropical storm threat churns planning for Georgia-Alabama game with Trump set to attend
entries.snippet: Tropical Storm Isaias could make landfall on the U.S. Gulf Coast as a hurricane this weekend, hours before No. 2 Georgia plays at No. 6 Alabama in a major college football game on Saturday night that President Donald Trump is planning to attend.

entries.title: Trump's $90 Medicare rebate rolls out, but millions aren't eligible. Critics see a political stunt
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump says his administration will make one-time payments of $90 per person to help more than 20 million Medicare enrollees pay for their Part B premiums. It will cost about $2 billion.

entries.title: WATCH LIVE: Winner of the 2026 Nobel Prize in literature is ...
entries.snippet: The Nobel Prize in literature will be announced Thursday.

entries.title: Flight attendants' union raises safety concerns over Trump's Washington arch
entries.snippet: The union representing thousands of flight attendants said Wednesday it has safety concerns about President Donald Trump's proposed triumphal arch that will be on final approach to Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport.

entries.title: Trump's executive order on dyed diesel will offer little relief, farmers and truckers say
entries.snippet: Farmers, truckers and economists say a move to cut taxes on diesel will provide little relief from record-high fuel prices that have soared since the U.S. attacked Iran months ago.

entries.title: WATCH: Rubio urges Europe to defend Western values and strengthen U.S. alliance in Greece

entries.title: Trump administration proposes a $70,000 fee for international students to work in the U.S.
entries.snippet: The Department of Homeland Security on Wednesday proposed a $70,000 fee for international students seeking to work in the United States, the latest effort from the Trump administration to crack down on foreign enrollment.

entries.title: DNC files lawsuit alleging Trump's taxpayer-funded ads are illegal propaganda
entries.snippet: The Democratic National Committee on Wednesday sued President Donald Trump's administration for recent television advertisements that promoted his political message while costing taxpayers millions of dollars.

entries.title: FBI says it stopped a Mall of America terror attack by a teen after agents sold him an assault rifle
entries.snippet: FBI agents thwarted a terror attack by a teenager on the Mall of America after monitoring him for nearly two years and ultimately supplying him with the assault rifle he planned to use, authorities said Wednesday.

entries.title: Shock gloves purchased by ICE cause pain, compliance and fear, Army study found
entries.snippet: The shock gloves immigration agents could soon use to control detainees and protesters worked so powerfully during a military exercise that participants felt intense pain, stopped fighting immediately and feared additional exposures, according to a previously unreleased Army stud

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Christa Pike 'angry and confused' after botched execution
entries.snippet: Pike's lawyers have said she was very aware of Tennessee's failed execution effort. A judge has ordered state officials to preserve all evidence from the botched execution.

entries.title: As US midterm elections loom, Trump's campaign tactics are becoming increasingly unusual, and expensive
entries.snippet: Despite not being on the ballot, Trump is campaigning hard ahead of the upcoming midterm elections. His tactics and promises have mostly been at the expense of US taypayers. Experts say some might violate federal law.

entries.title: Evicted Spanish pensioner who sparked housing protests has died, Madrid tenant union says
entries.snippet: Maricarmen ⁠Abascal, the octogenarian woman whose eviction set off housing protests across Spain, has died, a tenants' union in Madrid has said. Unions are now calling for a nationwide general strike on November 11.

entries.title: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Turkey: Could the Mecca defense pact become a game changer in the war against the Houthis in Yemen?
entries.snippet: Pakistan and Turkey have agreed to provide "practical measures" to defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks. Could a new alliance reshape the war against the Houthis in Yemen?

entries.title: Russia: WHO not able to 'fully' assess plague situation
entries.snippet: The UN health agency said Russia should be more transparent about the case of the plague as reports of a second case of the disease emerged. Russia played down any concerns, saying the population faces no risk.

entries.title: Gerhard Schröder visits latest Russian employer, Hyperglobus
entries.snippet: Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder visited a Moscow supermarket in his new role on the supervisory board. Schröder is no stranger to retirement stipends in Russia — or the scandal that accompanies them.

entries.title: German politicians warn of antisemitism on October 7 anniversary
entries.snippet: Leading German politicians including Chancellor Merz and President Steinmeier called for people to reject antisemitism.

entries.title: Transgressive, edgy DIY: What the 90s meant for British art
entries.snippet: The 1990s are remembered for Britpop and provocative fashion, but beyond the nostalgia, it was a decade of cultural experimentation and social change. Tate Britain's new exhibition looks past the familiar icons.

entries.title: Germany news: Merz rails against extremism, AfD sympathizers
entries.snippet: Political extremism threatens Germany's existing social order, Chancellor Merz has said. The Transport Ministry has proposed a five-year plan to improve Germany's ailing railroad infrastructure. DW has more.

entries.title: EU enlargement: European Commission tables reforms to prepare bloc for new members
entries.snippet: The European Commission is proposing earlier access to EU markets for candidate countries, new voting rules to reduce vetoes and extra safeguards for a bigger bloc. But is the reform fair — or even feasible?

entries.title: Why music in Iran is more than just entertainment
entries.snippet: Iranian authorities are trying to persuade prominent singers in exile to return home. While the state seeks to harness music as a political tool, music has also become a powerful expression of dissent and resistance.

entries.title: South Sudan's road to elections remains uncertain
entries.snippet: South Sudan's first general election is set for December 22. Insecurity, political tensions and the failure to begin voter registration have raised doubts over whether a credible poll can be held.

entries.title: China's Golden Week reveals cautious consumer spending despite travel surge
entries.snippet: Chinese visitors are returning from trips after the 13-day Golden Week holiday. Their subdued spending has raised fresh questions about domestic demand in the world's second-largest economy.

entries.title: German spy scandal threatens national security
entries.snippet: The arrest of Germany's former intelligence chief August Hanning could undermine national security, experts warn, as allies may reconsider their intelligence relationships.

entries.title: France suspends use of stun grenades against protesters
entries.snippet: France suspended the use of stun grenades against protesters as allegations of student brutality draw more anger. French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the country could not ignore students' concerns.

entries.title: Germany: Ex-spy chief sent to pretrial detention on treason charges
entries.snippet: August Hanning has been remanded into pretrial detention after his arrest. The case has prompted calls for transparency when spies leave the government.

entries.title: Germany: Did CDU lawmakers support the far-right AfD?
entries.snippet: Lawmakers of the center-right CDU may have voted for the far-right AfD candidate for parliamentary speaker in Saxony-Anhalt. Germany's Social Democrats warn of a "unique breach of taboos."

entries.title: Nobel Prize in Chemistry goes to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai
entries.snippet: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their groundbreaking discoveries related to the origin of chirality and life's building blocks.

entries.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
entries.snippet: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.
